title: A Record Year for Travel, but Closer to Home

source.author: Open Jaw
source.title: Record Year for Global Travel Defined by Tough Shoppers, Shorter Trips
source.checked_against: Travel Tomorrow, Ada Wein, 9 November 2026: https://traveltomorrow.com/global-travel-set-to-break-records-in-2026-despite-wars-and-rising-costs/ — agrees on 1.57 billion arrivals, +2% vs 2025, Middle East -40% this year, Europe +5% this year, 2027 +8% and Middle East +43% if conflict eases, 2.2 billion by 2032, the Goodger quote, and release at the opening of WTM London. The value-for-money, relax, AI and Gulf transit figures appear only in Open Jaw (single source). Spending totals left out: the two sources give them in different currencies and do not state the base year.

figures.text: report released 3 November at the start of WTM London
figures.quote: The report, produced with Tourism Economics, was released on 03NOV at the start of WTM London.

figures.text: report covers more than 185 countries; made by Tourism Economics
figures.quote: Tourism Economics, an Oxford Economics company, compiled the data for the report, which covers more than 185 countries

figures.text: 1.57 billion international overnight arrivals in 2026, +2% from 2025
figures.quote: It forecasts 1.57 billion international overnight arrivals this year, a 2% increase from 2025.

figures.text: arrivals growth 2% in 2025, down from 6% the year before
figures.quote: Arrivals growth dropped to 2% in 2025 from 6% the previous year.

figures.text: reasons: Iran conflict, higher jet fuel prices, cost of living
figures.quote: Tourism Economics cites the Iran conflict, higher jet fuel prices, and the cost of living as reasons.
Overnight arrivals to the Middle East dropped 40% in 2026.

figures.text: Gulf hubs handled 15% of global transit in 2025
figures.quote: Gulf hubs managed 15% of global transit in 2025.

figures.text: war closed airspace, blocking routes between Europe and Asia
figures.quote: much of the region's airspace was closed, blocking major routes between Europe and Asia

figures.text: travelers choose destinations closer to home
figures.quote: travellers are more selective, choosing destinations closer to home and using AI to compare prices
Europe, which is expected to see a 5% increase in international arrivals this year.

figures.text: one in six chose last destination for value in 2026, about one in 11 in 2025
figures.quote: In 2026, one in six chose their last international destination for value for money, up from about one in 11 in 2025.

figures.text: 56% interested in saving on some parts and spending more on others
figures.quote: 56% of survey respondents said they're interested in mixing the two, saving on some parts of a trip and splurging on others.

figures.text: 37% say need to relax is main motivator, up from 31% in 2025
figures.quote: 37% said the need to disconnect and relax is their primary motivator, up from 31% in 2025.

figures.text: AI: 58% search/compare prices, 53% recommendations, 36% complete a booking
figures.quote: 58% would use AI to search and compare prices, 53% would consider it for recommendations, and 36% would trust it to complete a booking.
If this year's disruption eases, international arrivals are forecast to grow 8% in 2027

figures.text: Middle East +43% in 2027 if Iran conflict ends
figures.quote: The report predicts a 43% rebound in 2027 if the conflict in Iran ends.
Growth of around 6% a year after that would take arrivals to 2.2 billion by 2032.

figures.text: Dave Goodger, Tourism Economics: travelers more active than ever, adapting how and where
figures.quote: "Travellers are more active in 2026 than ever before. Leisure travel remains a key priority in consumer budgets, even as travellers are adapting how and where they visit"

figures.text: industry on course for another record year despite disruption
figures.quote: the industry is on course for another record year in 2026," he added.

gather.en: to come together in one place

event.en: something planned that many people go to

come out.en: to be shown to the public for the first time

overnight.en: staying for one night or more

visitor.en: a person who comes to see a place

conflict.en: a fight or war between countries or groups

living.en: the way you live and pay for life

transit.en: passing through a place on the way to another place

airport.en: a place where planes land and take off

passenger.en: a person who travels in a car, plane or train

handle.en: to deal with or take care of

winner.en: a person or place that does better than others

careful.en: thinking a lot before you do something

motivation.en: the reason you want to do something

recommendation.en: an idea about what is good to do or buy

trust.en: to believe that someone or something is good and right

ease.en: to become less hard or less strong

calm.en: quiet, with no worry or noise

Dave Goodger.vi: giám đốc điều hành khu vực châu Âu, Trung Đông và châu Phi của Tourism Economics
